subject: maths
text: Let $\alpha,\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2-3x+r=0$, and $\dfrac{\alpha}{2},2\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2+3x+r=0$. If the roots of the equation $x^2+6x=m$ are $2\alpha+\beta+2r$ and $\alpha-2\beta-\dfrac r2$, then $m$ is equal to:
solution: $\alpha+\beta=3$ and $\alpha/2+2\beta=-3$ give $\beta=-3,\alpha=6$, $r=\alpha\beta=-18$. Roots of $x^2+6x-m=0$: $2\alpha+\beta+2r=-27$ and $\alpha-2\beta-r/2=21$ (sum $-6$ checks). Product $=-m=-567$, so $m=567$.

subject: maths
text: Let the circles $C_1:|z|=r$ and $C_2:|z-3-4i|=5$, $z\in\mathbb C$, be such that $C_2$ lies within $C_1$. If $z_1$ moves on $C_1$, $z_2$ moves on $C_2$ and $\min|z_1-z_2|=2$, then $\max|z_1-z_2|$ is equal to:
solution: $|3+4i|=5$, so $C_2$ passes through the origin; $C_1$ is concentric-offset: $\min=r-(5+5)=2\Rightarrow r=12$. $\max=r+10=22$.

subject: maths
text: If the system of equations $x+5y+6z=4$, $2x+3y+4z=7$, $x+6y+az=b$ has infinitely many solutions, then the point $(a,b)$ lies on the line
solution: $\Delta=-7a+50=0\Rightarrow a=50/7$. Writing row 3 $=\lambda R_1+\mu R_2$ gives $\lambda=9/7,\mu=-1/7$, so consistency needs $b=4\lambda+7\mu=29/7$. Then $a-b=3$.

subject: maths
text: Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ be an A.P. and $g_1=a_1,g_2,g_3,\ldots$ be an increasing G.P. If $a_1=a_2+g_2=1$ and $a_3+g_3=4$, then $a_{10}+g_5$ is equal to:
solution: With common ratio $r$, $a_2=1-r$ so $d=-r$; $a_3+g_3=1-2r+r^2=4\Rightarrow r=3$ (increasing). $a_{10}=1-27=-26$, $g_5=81$; sum $=55$.

subject: maths
text: The sum $\dfrac{1^3}{1}+\dfrac{1^3+2^3}{1+3}+\dfrac{1^3+2^3+3^3}{1+3+5}+\cdots$ up to 8 terms, is:

subject: maths
text: If for $3\le r\le 30$, $\left({}^{30}C_{30-r}\right)+3\left({}^{30}C_{31-r}\right)+3\left({}^{30}C_{32-r}\right)+\left({}^{30}C_{33-r}\right)={}^mC_r$, then $m$ equals:

subject: maths
text: Let $p_n$ denote the total number of triangles formed by joining the vertices of an $n$-side regular polygon. If $p_{n+1}-p_n=66$, then the sum of all distinct prime divisors of $n$ is:
solution: $p_n={}^nC_3$; $p_{n+1}-p_n={}^nC_2=66\Rightarrow n=12=2^2\cdot3$. Sum of distinct primes $=5$.

subject: maths
text: A man throws a fair coin repeatedly. He gets 10 points for each head he throws and 5 points for each tail he throws. If the probability that he gets exactly 30 points is $\dfrac mn$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to:
solution: In units of 5 points each toss adds 1 or 2 with probability $\tfrac12$. $P_k=\tfrac12(P_{k-1}+P_{k-2})$, $P_0=1,P_{-1}=0$: $P_1=\tfrac12,P_2=\tfrac34,P_3=\tfrac58,P_4=\tfrac{11}{16},P_5=\tfrac{21}{32},P_6=\tfrac{43}{64}$. $m+n=107$.

subject: maths
text: The mean and variance of $n$ observations are 8 and 16, respectively. If the sum of the first $(n-1)$ observations is 48 and the sum of squares of the first $(n-1)$ observations is 496, then the value of $n$ is:
solution: $\sum x=8n$, $\sum x^2=n(16+64)=80n$. Last observation $x=8n-48$ and $496+x^2=80n$ gives $4n^2-53n+175=0$, so $n=7$ (other root $25/4$ rejected).

subject: maths
text: Let a circle pass through the origin and its centre be the point of intersection of two mutually perpendicular lines $x+(k-1)y+3=0$ and $2x+k^2y-4=0$. If the line $x-y+2=0$ intersects the circle at the points $A$ and $B$, then $(AB)^2$ is equal to:
solution: Perpendicular: $2+(k-1)k^2=0\Rightarrow k=-1$. Lines $x-2y+3=0$, $2x+y-4=0$ meet at $(1,2)$; $r^2=5$. Distance to $x-y+2=0$ is $1/\sqrt2$, so $AB^2=4(5-\tfrac12)=18$.

subject: maths
text: Let $O$ be the origin, and $P$ and $Q$ be two points on the rectangular hyperbola $xy=12$ such that the mid point of the line segment $PQ$ is $\left(\dfrac12,-\dfrac12\right)$. Then the area of the triangle $OPQ$ equals:

subject: maths
text: Let the parabola $y=x^2+px+q$ passing through the point $(1,-1)$ be such that the distance between its vertex and the $x$-axis is minimum. Then the value of $p^2+q^2$ is:
solution: $q=-2-p$. Vertex ordinate $=q-p^2/4=-\left(\tfrac p2+1\right)^2-1$, distance $=\left(\tfrac p2+1\right)^2+1$ minimum at $p=-2$, $q=0$. $p^2+q^2=4$.

subject: maths
text: Let $P=\{\theta\in[0,4\pi]:\tan^2\theta\ne1\}$ and $S=\{a\in\mathbb Z:2(\cos^8\theta-\sin^8\theta)\sec2\theta=a^2,\ \theta\in P\}$. Then $n(S)$ is:
solution: $\cos^8\theta-\sin^8\theta=\cos2\theta\left(1-\tfrac12\sin^22\theta\right)$, so the expression is $2-\sin^22\theta$. Since $\tan^2\theta\ne1$ means $\sin^22\theta\ne1$, the range is $(1,2]$, which contains no perfect square. $n(S)=0$.

subject: maths
text: Let the vectors $\vec a=-\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k$. For some $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb R$, let $\vec c=\lambda\vec a+\mu\vec b$. If $\vec c\cdot(3\hat i-6\hat j+2\hat k)=10$ and $\vec c\cdot(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)=-2$, then $|\vec c|^2$ is equal to:
solution: $-3\lambda-13\mu=10$ and $3\lambda+5\mu=-2$ give $\mu=-1,\lambda=1$. $\vec c=\vec a-\vec b=(-2,-2,2)$, $|\vec c|^2=12$.

subject: maths
text: Let the point $A$ be the foot of perpendicular drawn from the point $P(a,b,0)$ on the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-\alpha}{3}$. If the midpoint of the line segment $PA$ is $\left(0,\dfrac34,\dfrac{-1}{4}\right)$, then the value of $a^2+b^2+\alpha^2$ is equal to:
solution: $A=(1+2t,2+t,\alpha+3t)$. Midpoint gives $a=-1-2t$, $b=-\tfrac12-t$, $\alpha+3t=-\tfrac12$. $\vec{PA}\cdot(2,1,3)=2(2+4t)+(\tfrac52+2t)-\tfrac32=5+10t=0\Rightarrow t=-\tfrac12$. So $a=0,b=0,\alpha=1$; sum $=1$.

subject: maths
text: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram $PQRS$ are given by $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\hat j+\hat k$ and $\overrightarrow{PS}=\hat i-\hat j$. If the side $PS$ is rotated about the point $P$ by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that it becomes perpendicular to the side $PQ$, then $\sin^2\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}2\right)-\sin^2\left(\dfrac\alpha2\right)$ is equal to:
solution: $\cos\angle QPS=\dfrac{-1}{2}$, so the angle is $120^\circ$; to make it $90^\circ$ rotate by $\alpha=30^\circ$. $\sin^2A-\sin^2B=\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)=\sin3\alpha\sin2\alpha=\sin90^\circ\sin60^\circ=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2$.

subject: maths
text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{20\pi}(\sin^4x+\cos^4x)\,dx$ is equal to:
solution: $\sin^4x+\cos^4x=\tfrac34+\tfrac14\cos4x$; over $20\pi$ the cosine integrates to zero, giving $20\pi\cdot\tfrac34=15\pi$.

subject: maths
text: Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial of degree 5, and have extrema at $x=1$ and $x=-1$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{x^3}\right)=-5$, then $f(2)-f(-2)$ is equal to:

subject: maths
text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int\left(\dfrac{16x+24}{x^2+2x-15}\right)dx$. If $f(4)=14\log_e3$ and $f(7)=\log_e(2^\alpha\cdot3^\beta)$, $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to:
solution: Partial fractions: $\dfrac{7}{x+5}+\dfrac{9}{x-3}$, so $f=7\ln|x+5|+9\ln|x-3|+c$. $f(4)=14\ln3+c\Rightarrow c=0$. $f(7)=7\ln12+9\ln4=32\ln2+7\ln3$; $\alpha+\beta=39$.

subject: maths
text: Let $x=x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2y^2\dfrac{dx}{dy}-2xy+x^2=0$, $y>1$, $x(e)=e$. Then $x(e^2)$ is equal to:
solution: Put $x=vy$: $yv'=-v^2/2\Rightarrow \dfrac1v=\tfrac12\ln y+c$. $v(e)=1\Rightarrow c=\tfrac12$. At $y=e^2$: $1/v=\tfrac32$, $x=\tfrac23e^2$.

subject: maths
text: Let $A=\{2,3,4,5,6\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on the set $A\times A$ given by $(x,y)R(z,w)$ if and only if $x$ divides $z$ and $y\le w$. Then the number of elements in $R$ is ______.
solution: Pairs $(x,z)$ with $x\mid z$: $3+2+1+1+1=8$. Pairs $(y,w)$ with $y\le w$: $15$. Total $=8\times15=120$.

subject: maths
text: Consider the matrices $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-2\\4&-2\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}3&9\\1&3\end{bmatrix}$. If $P$ and $Q$ are matrices such that $PA=B$ and $AQ=B$, then the absolute value of the sum of the diagonal elements of $2(P+Q)$ is ______.
solution: $|A|=4$, $A^{-1}=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}-2&2\\-4&2\end{bmatrix}$. $P=BA^{-1}$ has trace $\tfrac{-42+8}{4}$; $Q=A^{-1}B$ has trace $\tfrac{-4-30}{4}$. $\mathrm{tr}(P+Q)=-17$, so $|2\,\mathrm{tr}(P+Q)|=34$.

subject: maths
text: Let $A$ be the point $(3,0)$ and circles with variable diameter $AB$ touch the circle $x^2+y^2=36$ internally. Let the curve $C$ be the locus of the point $B$. If the eccentricity of $C$ is $e$, then $72e^2$ is equal to ______.
solution: For the midpoint $M$ of $AB$: $OM=6-MA$, so $OM+MA=6$, an ellipse with foci $O,A$: $2a=6$, $2ae=3$, $e=\tfrac12$. Locus of $B$ is a scaled copy (factor 2) with the same $e$. $72e^2=18$.

subject: maths
text: If the area of the region bounded by $16x^2-9y^2=144$ and $8x-3y=24$ is $A$, then $3(A+6\log_e3)$ is equal to ______.
solution: Line meets hyperbola $\tfrac{x^2}{9}-\tfrac{y^2}{16}=1$ at $(3,0)$ and $(5,\tfrac{16}{3})$. Area $=\int_3^5\left[\tfrac43\sqrt{x^2-9}-\tfrac{8x-24}{3}\right]dx=\left(\tfrac{40}{3}-6\ln3\right)-\tfrac{16}{3}=8-6\ln3$. So $3(A+6\ln3)=24$.

subject: maths
text: The number of points in the interval $[2,4]$, at which the function $f(x)=\left[\left|x^2-x-\tfrac12\right|\right]$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is discontinuous, is ______.
solution: $g=x^2-x-\tfrac12$ is increasing on $[2,4]$ from $1.5$ to $11.5$ and positive. $[g]$ jumps whenever $g$ crosses an integer: $g=2,3,\ldots,11$, i.e. 10 points.

subject: physics
text: Dimensions of universal gravitational constant ($G$) in terms of Planck's constant ($h$), distance ($L$), mass ($M$) and time ($T$) are ______.

subject: physics
text: A 0.5 kg mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius 4 m rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall (without falling) is 5 rad/s. The coefficient of friction between the drum's inner wall surface and mass is ______. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
solution: $N=m\omega^2r$, $\mu N=mg\Rightarrow\mu=\dfrac{g}{\omega^2r}=\dfrac{10}{25\times4}=0.1$.

subject: physics
text: Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 1 kg respectively, are tied to the ends of a string which passes over a light frictionless pulley (the blocks hang on either side of the pulley, as shown in the figure). The masses are held at rest at the same horizontal level and then released. The distance traversed by the centre of mass in 2 s is ______ m. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
solution: Atwood: $a=\dfrac{(2-1)g}{3}=\dfrac g3$. $a_{cm}=\dfrac{2a-1a}{3}=\dfrac a3=\dfrac g9$. $s=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{10}{9}\cdot4=\tfrac{20}{9}=2.22$ m.

subject: physics
chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
text: A particle having charge $10^{-9}$ C moving in $x$-$y$ plane in fields of $0.4\,\hat j$ N/C and $4\times10^{-3}\,\hat k$ T experiences a force of $(4\hat i+2\hat j)\times10^{-10}$ N. The velocity of the particle at that instant is ______ m/s.
solution: $\vec F/q=0.4\hat i+0.2\hat j=\vec E+\vec v\times\vec B$, so $\vec v\times\vec B=0.4\hat i-0.2\hat j$. With $\vec B=B\hat k$: $\vec v\times\vec B=B(v_y\hat i-v_x\hat j)$ giving $v_y=100$, $v_x=50$.

subject: physics
text: If $X$ and $Y$ are the inputs, the given circuit works as ______. (Circuit: $X$ and $Y$ each feed both inputs of a separate NAND gate; the outputs of these two NAND gates feed a third NAND gate; its output feeds both inputs of a fourth NAND gate, whose output is the circuit output.)
solution: The first two gates act as NOT: $\bar X,\bar Y$. The third gives $\overline{\bar X\bar Y}=X+Y$. The last (inputs tied) inverts it: $\overline{X+Y}$, a NOR gate.

subject: physics
text: If a body of mass 1 kg falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity ($v$) and kinetic energy ($k$) on reaching the surface of earth. The values of $v$ and $k$ respectively are ______. (Take radius of earth to be 6400 km and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$)
solution: $v=\sqrt{2gR}=\sqrt{2\times9.8\times6.4\times10^6}=11.2$ km/s; $K=\tfrac12mv^2=gRm=6.27\times10^7$ J.

subject: physics
text: In a screw gauge the zero of main scale reference line coincides with the fifth division of the circular scale when two studs are in contact. There are 100 divisions in circular scale and pitch of screw gauge is 0.1 mm. When diameter of a sphere is measured, the reading of main scale is 5 mm and 50th division of circular scale coincides with the reference line of main scale. The diameter of sphere is ______ mm.

subject: physics
text: The surface tension of a soap bubble is 0.03 N/m. The work done in increasing the diameter of bubble from 2 cm to 6 cm is $\alpha\pi\times10^{-4}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ______. (Take $\pi=3.14$)

subject: physics
text: A mixture of carbon dioxide and oxygen has volume 8310 cm$^3$, temperature 300 K, pressure 100 kPa and mass 13.2 g. The number of moles of carbon dioxide and oxygen gases in the mixture respectively are ______. (Assume both behave like ideal gases) [$R=8.31$ J/mol.K]
solution: $n=\dfrac{PV}{RT}=\dfrac{10^5\times8.31\times10^{-3}}{8.31\times300}=\tfrac13$. $x+y=\tfrac13$, $44x+32y=13.2\Rightarrow x=0.21,y=0.12$.

subject: physics
text: If an air bubble of diameter 2 mm rises steadily through a liquid of density 2000 kg/m$^3$ at a rate of 0.5 cm/s, then the coefficient of viscosity of liquid is ______ Poise. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
solution: Neglecting air density, $\eta=\dfrac{2r^2\rho g}{9v}=\dfrac{2\times10^{-6}\times2000\times10}{9\times0.005}\approx0.89$ Pa s $\approx8.8$ poise.

subject: physics
text: A spherical ball of mass 2 kg falls from a height of 10 m and is brought to rest after penetrating 10 cm into sand. The average force exerted by sand on the ball is ______ N. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
solution: Work-energy over the whole motion: $mg(10+0.1)=F(0.1)\Rightarrow F=\dfrac{2\times10\times10.1}{0.1}=2020$ N.

subject: physics
text: An electromagnetic wave travels in free space along the $x$-direction. At a particular point in space and time, $\vec B=2\times10^{-7}\,\hat j$ T is associated with this wave. The value of corresponding electric field $\vec E$ at this point is ______ V/m.
solution: $E=cB=3\times10^8\times2\times10^{-7}=60$ V/m. Direction: $\vec E\times\vec B\parallel+\hat i$; $(-\hat k)\times\hat j=\hat i$, so $\vec E=-60\hat k$.

subject: physics
text: Two resistors of 200 $\Omega$ and 400 $\Omega$ are connected in series with a battery of 100 V. A bulb rated at 200 V, 100 W is connected across the 400 $\Omega$ resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is ______ V.
solution: Bulb resistance $=200^2/100=400\ \Omega$; parallel with 400 $\Omega$ gives 200 $\Omega$. Series with 200 $\Omega$ splits 100 V equally: 50 V.

subject: physics
text: Two metal plates ($A$, $B$) are kept horizontally with separation of $\left(\dfrac{12}{\pi}\right)$ cm, with plate $A$ on the top. An atomizer jet sprays oil (density 1.5 g/cm$^3$) droplets of radius 1 mm horizontally. All oil droplets carry a charge 5 nC. The potentials $V_A$ and $V_B$ are required on plates $A$ and $B$ respectively in order to ensure the droplets do not descend. The values of $V_A$ and $V_B$ are ______. (Neglect the air resistance and take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
solution: $mg=\tfrac43\pi(10^{-3})^3(1500)(10)=2\pi\times10^{-5}$ N. Need $qE=mg$ upward: $E=4000\pi$ V/m, $\Delta V=Ed=4000\pi\times\tfrac{0.12}{\pi}=480$ V with $B$ higher than $A$. Only option 1 has $V_B-V_A=480$ V.

subject: physics
text: Two point charges $8\ \mu$C and $-2\ \mu$C are located at $x=2$ cm and $x=4$ cm, respectively on the $x$-axis. The ratio of electric flux due to these charges through two spheres of radii 3 cm and 5 cm with their centers at the origin is ______.
solution: The 3 cm sphere encloses only the $8\ \mu$C charge; the 5 cm sphere encloses both, net $6\ \mu$C. Ratio $=8:6=4:3$.

subject: physics
text: One side of an equilateral prism is painted by a transparent material of refractive index $n_2$. The refractive index of prism is 1.6. The minimum value of $n_2$ required for total internal reflection from painted face is ______. (Figure: a ray enters the left face of the prism normally and strikes the painted base.)
solution: Ray enters the left face normally and meets the base at incidence angle $60^\circ$. TIR needs $1.6\sin60^\circ\ge n_2$, i.e. the critical value is $n_2=0.8\sqrt3=4\sqrt3/5$ (wording 'minimum' is really the limiting value; only this option matches).

subject: physics
text: The figure shows an LCR series circuit with two switches $S_1$ and $S_2$ (source $v=V_0\sin(300t)$, $C=100\ \mu$F, resistance $R$, inductors $L_1$ and $L_2$; closing $S_1$ puts $L_2$ out of the circuit leaving $C$, $R$, $L_1$ in series, closing $S_2$ puts $L_1$ out leaving $C$, $R$, $L_2$ in series). When switch $S_1$ is closed keeping $S_2$ open, the phase difference ($\phi$) between the current and source voltage is $30^\circ$ and phase difference is $60^\circ$ when $S_2$ is closed keeping $S_1$ open. The value of $(3L_1-L_2)$ is ______ H.
solution: $X_C=1/(300\times10^{-4})$. $\omega L_1-X_C=R\tan30^\circ$, $\omega L_2-X_C=R\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3R$. Then $3\omega L_1-\omega L_2=2X_C$, so $3L_1-L_2=\dfrac{2}{\omega^2C}=\dfrac{2}{9\times10^4\times10^{-4}}=\dfrac29$ H.

subject: physics
text: A circular current loop of radius $R$ is placed inside square loop of side length $L$ ($L\gg R$) such that they are co-planar and their centers coincide. The permeability of free space is $\mu_0$. The mutual inductance between circular loop and square loop is ______.
solution: Current $I$ in the square gives $B$ at centre $=4\cdot\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi(L/2)}\cdot\sqrt2=\dfrac{2\sqrt2\mu_0I}{\pi L}$. Flux through small loop $=B\pi R^2$, so $M=\dfrac{2\sqrt2\mu_0R^2}{L}$.

subject: physics
text: The equation of motion of a particle is given by $x=a\sin\left(50t+\dfrac\pi3\right)$ cm. The particle will come to rest at time $t_1$ and it will have zero acceleration at time $t_2$. The $t_1$ and $t_2$ respectively are ______.
solution: At rest: $\cos(50t+\pi/3)=0\Rightarrow50t+\pi/3=\pi/2$, $t_1=\pi/300$. Zero acceleration: $\sin(50t+\pi/3)=0\Rightarrow50t+\pi/3=\pi$, $t_2=\pi/75$ (first occurrences).

subject: physics
text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at some point on the screen is found to be $\dfrac34$ times of the maximum of the interference pattern. The path difference between the interfering waves at this point is $\dfrac\lambda x$ where $\lambda$ is wavelength of the incident light. The value of $x$ is ______.
solution: $I=I_0\cos^2(\phi/2)=\tfrac34I_0\Rightarrow\phi=60^\circ$ (smallest). Path difference $=\dfrac{\phi}{2\pi}\lambda=\dfrac\lambda6$, so $x=6$.

subject: physics
text: Using Bohr's model, calculate the ratio of the magnetic fields generated due to the motion of the electrons in the $2^{nd}$ and $4^{th}$ orbits of hydrogen atom ______.
solution: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2r}$ at the nucleus with $I=ef\propto n^{-3}$ and $r\propto n^2$, so $B\propto n^{-5}$. $B_2/B_4=(4/2)^5=32$.

subject: physics
text: 5 moles of unknown gas is heated at constant volume from $10^\circ$C to $20^\circ$C. The molar specific heat of this gas at constant pressure $c_p=8$ cal/mol.$^\circ$C and $R=8.36$ J/mol.$^\circ$C. The change in the internal energy of the gas is ______ calorie.
solution: $R=8.36/4.18=2$ cal/mol K, $C_v=8-2=6$. $\Delta U=nC_v\Delta T=5\times6\times10=300$ cal.

subject: physics
text: If sunlight is focused on a paper using convex lens, it starts burning the paper in shortest time when the lens is kept at 30 cm above the paper. If the radius of curvature of the lens is 60 cm then the refractive index of the lens material is $\dfrac{\alpha}{10}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
solution: Paper at focus: $f=30$ cm. For a biconvex lens with both radii 60 cm, $\dfrac1f=(\mu-1)\dfrac2R\Rightarrow\dfrac1{30}=(\mu-1)\dfrac1{30}$, $\mu=2$, $\alpha=20$. (Assumes equiconvex lens.)

subject: physics
text: Moment of inertia about an axis $AB$ for a rod of mass 40 kg and length 3 m is same as that of a solid sphere of mass of 10 kg and radius $R$ about an axis parallel to $AB$ axis with separation of 3 m as shown in figure. The value of $R$ is given as $\sqrt{\dfrac\alpha2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______. (Figure: the rod lies perpendicular to the vertical axis $AB$ with one end on the axis; the sphere centre is 3 m from the parallel axis.)

subject: chemistry
text: The ratio of mass percentage (w/w) of C : H in a hydrocarbon is $12:1$. It has two carbon atoms. The weight (in g) of $CO_2(g)$ formed when 3.38 g of this hydrocarbon is completely burnt in oxygen is: (Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16)

subject: chemistry
text: The first and second ionization constants of a weak dibasic acid $H_2A$ are $8.1\times10^{-8}$ and $1.0\times10^{-13}$ respectively. 0.1 mol of $H_2A$ was dissolved in 1 L of 0.1 M HCl solution. The concentration of $HA^-$ in the resultant solution is:
solution: $[H^+]\approx0.1$ (HCl) and $[H_2A]\approx0.1$: $[HA^-]=K_{a1}\dfrac{[H_2A]}{[H^+]}=8.1\times10^{-8}$ M; second ionization is negligible.

subject: chemistry
text: $SF_4$ is isostructural with: A. $BrF_4^-$  B. $CH_4$  C. $IF_4^+$  D. $XeF_4$  E. $XeO_2F_2$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: $SF_4$ is see-saw ($sp^3d$, one lone pair). $IF_4^+$ and $XeO_2F_2$ are also see-saw; $BrF_4^-$ and $XeF_4$ are square planar; $CH_4$ is tetrahedral.

subject: chemistry
text: Gas 'A' undergoes change from state 'X' to state 'Y'. In this process, the heat absorbed and work done by the gas is 10 J and 18 J respectively. Now gas is brought back to state 'X' by another process during which 6 J of heat is evolved. In the reverse process of 'Y' to 'X',
solution: $X\to Y$: $\Delta U=10-18=-8$ J. $Y\to X$: $\Delta U=+8$ J, $q=-6$ J, so $w_{on}=\Delta U-q=8+6=14$ J done on the gas.
options: 18 J of the work is done by the gas 'A'.
2 J of the work is done by the gas 'A'.
12 J of the work is done on the gas 'A' by the surroundings.
14 J of the work is done on the gas 'A' by the surroundings.

subject: chemistry
text: Solution A is prepared by dissolving 1 g of a protein (molar mass $=50000$ g mol$^{-1}$) in 0.5 L of water at 300 K. Its osmotic pressure is $x$ bar. Solution B is made by dissolving 2 g of same protein in 1 L of water at 300 K. Osmotic pressure of solution B is $y$ bar. Entire solution of A is mixed with entire solution of B at same temperature. The osmotic pressure of resultant solution is $z$ bar. $x$, $y$ and $z$ respectively are: ($R=0.083$ L bar mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
solution: Both A and B have $C=4\times10^{-5}$ M. $\pi=CRT=4\times10^{-5}\times0.083\times300=9.96\times10^{-4}$ bar. Mixture: $6\times10^{-5}$ mol in 1.5 L, again $4\times10^{-5}$ M, so $z=9.96\times10^{-4}$ bar.

subject: chemistry
text: At $25^\circ$C, 20.0 mL of 0.2 M weak monoprotic acid HX is titrated against 0.2 M NaOH. The pH of the solution (a) at the start of the titration (when NaOH has not been added) and (b) when 10 mL of NaOH is added respectively, are: Given: $K_a=5\times10^{-4}$, $p K_a=3.3$, $\alpha\ll1$
solution: (a) $[H^+]=\sqrt{K_aC}=\sqrt{5\times10^{-4}\times0.2}=10^{-2}$, pH $=2.0$. (b) 10 mL NaOH is half-neutralisation, pH $=pK_a=3.3$.

subject: chemistry
text: Consider the reaction $aX\to bY$, for which the rate constant at $30^\circ$C is $1\times10^{-3}$ mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$. Which of the following statements are true? A. When concentration of 'X' is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes 16 times. B. The reaction is a second order reaction. C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X. D. Decomposition of $N_2O_5$ is an example of the above reaction. E. $\ln\dfrac{[R_0]}{[R]}$ vs time is a straight line through origin (rising line) and is valid for the above reaction.
solution: Units mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$ mean second order: A and B true. $t_{1/2}=1/(k[A]_0)$ depends on concentration (C false). $N_2O_5$ decomposition is first order (D false). $\ln([R]_0/[R])$ linear in $t$ is first-order behaviour (E false).
options: A, B, D and E Only

subject: chemistry
text: The correct set that contains all kinds (basic, acidic, amphoteric and neutral) of oxides is:
solution: $K_2O$ basic, $Cl_2O_7$ acidic, $As_2O_3$ amphoteric, $NO$ neutral: all four kinds. Other sets lack an acidic oxide (and some a basic one).

subject: chemistry
text: Statement I: The second ionization enthalpy of B, Al and Ga is in the order of B > Al > Ga. Statement II: The correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy is Si < Ge < Pb < Sn. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options below:
solution: $IE_2$ (kJ/mol): B 2427, Al 1817, Ga 1979, so Al < Ga: I false. $IE_1$: Si 786, Ge 762, Pb 716, Sn 709, so the true order is Sn < Pb < Ge < Si: II false.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: Statement I: Among Zn, Mn, Sc and Cu, the energy required to remove the third valence electron is highest for Zn and lowest for Sc. Statement II: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of CFSE is $[Co(H_2O)_6]^{2+}<[Co(H_2O)_6]^{3+}<[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
solution: $IE_3$ (kJ/mol): Zn 3833 (highest, removal from $d^{10}$), Cu 3555, Mn 3248, Sc 2388 (lowest): I true. CFSE magnitude: $Co^{2+}$ (weak field) $<[Co(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ (low spin, larger $\Delta_o$) $<[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$: II true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: Which of the following complexes will show coordination isomerism? A. $[Ag(NH_3)_2][Ag(CN)_2]$ B. $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$ C. $[Co(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]$ D. $[Fe(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]$ E. $[Co(NH_3)_6][Fe(CN)_6]$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: Coordination isomerism needs cationic and anionic complexes with ligand exchange between two different metal centres: B, D, E (different metals). A and C contain the same metal in both parts, so exchange gives an identical compound.

subject: chemistry
text: Complete combustion of $X$ g of an organic compound gave 0.25 g of $CO_2$ and 0.12 g of $H_2O$. If the % of carbon is 25% and of hydrogen is 4.89%, then $X=$ ______ $\times10^{-3}$ g. (Nearest integer) (Molar mass of C, H and O are 12, 1 and 16 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.)

subject: chemistry
text: Statement I: In $O_2N-C_6H_4-\overset{\oplus}{C}H-C_6H_4-OCH_3$ (both rings para-substituted), the carbocation is stabilised by $+R$ effect of $-OCH_3$ group. Statement II: In $O_2N-C_6H_4-\overset{\ominus}{C}H-C_6H_4-OCH_3$, the carbanion is stabilised by $-R$ effect of $-NO_2$ group. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
solution: The $-OCH_3$ is para on the ring bearing the cationic carbon, so its lone pair delocalises ($+R$) and stabilises the cation. The $-NO_2$ is para on the ring bearing the carbanion centre, so it delocalises negative charge ($-R$). Both true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: The compound (X): (i) on heating in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ and HCl gas gives 2,4-dimethyl pentane, (ii) aromatization gives toluene and (iii) cyclisation gives methyl cyclohexane. The correct name of compound (X) is:
solution: Isomerisation to branched $C_7H_{16}$ (2,4-dimethylpentane), aromatisation to toluene and cyclisation to methylcyclohexane are reactions of the saturated alkane n-heptane.

subject: chemistry
text: Correct statements regarding alkyl halides (R-X) among the following are: A. Alcohol being less polar solvent as compared to water, alcoholic KOH favours elimination reaction with R-X. B. Order of reactivity towards $S_N1$ mechanism is $C_6H_5CH_2Cl>C_6H_5CHCl-C_6H_5$. C. Non substituted aryl halides exhibit properties similar to alkyl halides. D. Vinyl chloride is an example of haloalkene and allyl chloride is an example of haloalkyne. E. R-Cl can be prepared by reacting R-OH with $SOCl_2$, but Ar-Cl cannot be prepared by reacting Ar-OH with $SOCl_2$.
solution: A true. B false: $(C_6H_5)_2CHCl$ gives the more stabilised cation, so it is more reactive in $S_N1$. C false. D false (allyl chloride is not a haloalkyne). E true (C-O bond in phenol has partial double bond character).

subject: chemistry
text: An organic compound 'x' where molar ratio of C, O and H are equal, on treatment with 50% KOH under reflux followed by acidification produced 'y'. The most likely structure of 'y' is: [Molar mass of 'x' is 58 g mol$^{-1}$]
solution: C:H:O $=1:1:1$ with $M=58$ gives $C_2H_2O_2$, glyoxal $OHC-CHO$. Having no $\alpha$-H, with conc. KOH it undergoes intramolecular Cannizzaro to $HOCH_2COO^-$, giving glycolic acid on acidification.

subject: chemistry
text: A molecule (X) with the following structure ($CH_3-CH=CH-O-C(CH_3)=CH_2$, a propenyl isopropenyl ether) under mild acidic condition is hydrolysed to produce (Y) and (Z). Identify the correct statements about (Y) and (Z). A. Both (Y) and (Z) have same molar mass. B. (Y) and (Z) can be distinguished from each other by $NaHCO_3$. C. (Y) and (Z) react with HCN with same rates. D. (Y) and (Z) undergo addition reaction with 2,4-DNP.
solution: Enol ether hydrolysis gives propanal ($M=58$) and acetone ($M=58$): A true. Neither is acidic, so $NaHCO_3$ cannot distinguish (B false). Aldehyde reacts faster with HCN (C false). Both carbonyls react with 2,4-DNP (D true).

subject: chemistry
text: Identify compounds A and E in the reaction sequence: p-nitroethylbenzene $\xrightarrow{Br_2/AlBr_3}A\xrightarrow{Sn/HCl}B\xrightarrow{NaNO_2/HCl,\ 273-278\,K}C\xrightarrow{C_2H_5OH}D\xrightarrow{(i)KMnO_4/KOH,(ii)H_3O^+}E$. (Options give A and E as structures.)
solution: Br enters ortho to the activating ethyl (meta to $NO_2$): A. Sn/HCl gives the amine; diazotisation then $C_2H_5OH$ replaces $N_2^+$ by H (2-bromoethylbenzene); $KMnO_4$ oxidises the side chain to COOH: 2-bromobenzoic acid.
options: A = 3-bromo-1-ethyl-4-nitrobenzene (Br ortho to NO2); E = 3-bromobenzoic acid

subject: chemistry
text: Identify the correct pair having amino acid (A) and the hormone (B) that is iodinated derivative of the amino acid (A). (T and Y represent one letter code for amino acids)
solution: Thyroxine is the iodinated derivative of tyrosine (one-letter code Y); T is threonine.

subject: chemistry
text: Among $Fe^{2+}$, $Fe^{3+}$, $Cr^{2+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$, the ion that shows positive borax bead test and with highest ionisation enthalpy is:
solution: $Zn^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$) is colourless and gives no bead colour; $Fe^{2+},Fe^{3+},Cr^{2+}$ give coloured beads. Ionisation enthalpy of the next electron is highest for the half-filled $d^5$ ion $Fe^{3+}$.

subject: chemistry
text: The surface of sodium metal is irradiated with radiation of wavelength $x$ nm. The kinetic energy of ejected electrons is $2.8\times10^{-20}$ J. The work function of sodium is 2.3 eV. The value of $x$ is ______ $\times10^2$ nm. (Nearest integer) (Given: $h=6.6\times10^{-34}$ J s; 1 eV $=1.6\times10^{-19}$ J; $c=3.0\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$)

subject: chemistry
text: Consider the following gas phase reaction being carried out in a closed vessel at $25^\circ$C: $2A(g)\to4B(g)+C(g)$. Total pressure of the system: 300 mm Hg at 30 min and 600 mm Hg at $\infty$. The pressure of $C(g)$ at 30 minutes time interval would be ______ mm Hg. (nearest integer)
solution: Initial $P_A=P_0$; at $\infty$: $P_0\cdot\tfrac52=600\Rightarrow P_0=240$. At 30 min with $x=P_C$: $P_{total}=240+3x=300\Rightarrow x=20$ mm Hg.

subject: chemistry
text: Consider two half-cell reactions: $CO_2+6H^++6e^-\to CH_3OH+H_2O$, $E^\circ_{red}=0.02$ V; $\tfrac12O_2+2H^++2e^-\to H_2O$, $E^\circ_{red}=1.23$ V. A fuel cell was set up using the above two reactions under standard conditions of 1 bar and 298 K. The fuel cell works with 80% efficiency. If the work derived from the cell using 1 mol of $CH_3OH$ is used to compress an ideal gas isothermally against a constant pressure of 1 kPa, then the change in the volume of the gas, $\Delta V=$ ______ m$^3$. (nearest integer) Given: $F=96500$ C mol$^{-1}$
solution: $E^\circ_{cell}=1.23-0.02=1.21$ V, $n=6$. $\Delta G=-6\times96500\times1.21=-7.006\times10^5$ J. Usable work $=0.8\times7.006\times10^5=5.60\times10^5$ J $=P|\Delta V|=10^3|\Delta V|$, so $|\Delta V|\approx560$ m$^3$ (a compression, $\Delta V=-560$).

subject: chemistry
text: Number of paramagnetic ions among the following d- and f-block metal ions is ______. $Mn^{2+}$, $Cu^{2+}$, $Zn^{2+}$, $Yb^{2+}$, $Sc^{3+}$, $La^{3+}$, $Gd^{3+}$, $Lu^{3+}$, $Ti^{4+}$, $Ce^{4+}$ (Atomic number of Mn = 25, Cu = 29, Zn = 30, Yb = 70, Sc = 21, La = 57, Gd = 64, Lu = 71, Ti = 22, Ce = 58)

subject: chemistry
text: Consider the reaction sequence: p-nitrotoluene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Sn/HCl; OH}^-,\ \text{(ii) }(CH_3CO)_2O,\ \text{(iii) }Br_2/AlBr_3,\ \text{(iv) }H_3O^+}$ Major Product (P). When the product (P) is subjected to Carius analysis using $AgNO_3$, 1.0 g of the product (P) will produce ______ g of the precipitate of AgBr. (Nearest Integer) (Given: molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, N : 14, Br : 80, Ag : 108)
solution: Reduction gives p-toluidine, acetylation gives the acetanilide, bromination occurs ortho to $-NHCOCH_3$, and acid hydrolysis gives 2-bromo-4-methylaniline ($C_7H_8BrN$, $M=186$). 1.0 g gives $1/186$ mol AgBr $=188/186\approx1.01\approx1$ g.
